subtopics.title: The Vocabulary of the Circle and the Chord Theorems

questions.question: In the proof that the perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord, the congruency condition used is:
A chord of length 16 lies in a circle of radius 10. Its distance from the centre is:
The chord-distance triangle is built from the distance, a radius, and:
The perpendicular bisector of any chord always:
options: Has the same length as the radius

subtopics.title: The Angle at the Centre Is Double the Angle at the Circumference

questions.question: If the angle at the centre on an arc is 140°, the angle at the circumference on the same arc is:
The proof of the centre-double theorem uses isosceles triangles and:
options: The exterior angle of a triangle

questions.question: If the reflex angle at the centre is 220°, the circumference angle standing on that same far arc is:
The angle in a semicircle is 90° because:
options: The radius is perpendicular to the diameter
The two base angles are equal
The central angle on a diameter is 180°, and the circumference angle is half of it

questions.question: Angles subtended by the same chord on the same side of it are:
The one-line proof of the same-segment theorem says both angles equal:
options: Half the central angle on the same arc

questions.question: Chord AB subtends 53° at C; D lies on the same arc as C. Angle ADB is:
If two vertices sit on opposite sides of the chord, their subtended angles are:
options: Not equal — that case belongs to cyclic quadrilaterals

subtopics.title: Riders — Reading the Diagram and Writing Reasons

questions.question: In CAPS marking, a correct statement without a reason earns:
With angle AOB = 100° at the centre on minor arc AB and C on the major arc, angle ACB is:
In the same rider, the base angles of isosceles triangle AOB are each:
If BC is a diameter and angle ACB = 50°, then angle ABC equals:
Folding a paper circle so a chord's endpoints meet produces a crease that:
options: Bisects the chord at right angles and passes through the centre
Touches the circle at one point
Halves the circle's area but misses the centre

questions.question: Two such folds are enough to find:
The classic lost mark in chord-distance sums is:
options: Using the diameter instead of the radius
Using the whole chord in the right-angled triangle instead of half of it

subtopics.title: The Whole Stadium Sees the Same Game

questions.question: Seats along the same curved stand, on one side of the goal-chord, see the goal mouth at:
options: Angles that shrink towards the ends

questions.question: If the centre sees the goal at 140°, a seat on the far curve sees it at:
When the goal-chord is a full diameter, every seat on the curve sees it at:
The stadium rule that stops the theorem misfiring is:
options: The seat and the centre must be watching the same arc
The seat must be opposite the centre

subtopics.title: Solving a Rider Like a Case File

questions.question: The first move on any rider diagram with a marked centre is to:
options: Darken every radius — two radii make an isosceles triangle
Measure the angles with a protractor

questions.question: A diameter in a rider is valuable because it:
options: Plants a free 90° angle at the circumference

questions.question: In the worked case, the 100° centre angle led to base angles of 40° because:
options: The isosceles triangle's remaining 80° splits equally between the two base angles

questions.question: An answer with no reasons is compared to:
options: A suspect with no evidence — it walks away with nothing
